topic: The Essence of Calculus: From Discrete to Continuous
target_audience: High school students or introductory university students

sections.title: The Hook: The Limits of Average
lecture_lines: Average speed doesn't reveal speed at a moment.
It only tells us what happened over time.
We need a way to measure instantaneous change.
animations: Show a group of points with a calculated average #FFFFFF.
Show a dynamic point moving outside the average range #FF0000.
Highlight the discrepancy between local change and total average #00FF00.

sections.title: The Derivative: Magnifying the Instant
lecture_lines: We zoom in on the cheetah's position curve.
As we zoom, the curve looks straight.
This straight line represents instantaneous velocity.
animations: Draw a smooth curve #FFFFFF on the screen.
Zoom into a specific point on the curve #FFFF00.
Draw a tangent line at that point #00FFFF.

sections.title: The Integral: Summing the Infinite
lecture_lines: Calculating areas of curves is inherently difficult.
We approximate the area using tiny rectangles.
Summing these rectangles gives the total area.
animations: Display a curve #FFFFFF above the x-axis.
Fill the area under the curve with small rectangles #FF00FF.
Increase the number of rectangles to approximate the area #00FF00.

sections.title: The Fundamental Theorem: The Bridge
lecture_lines: Differentiation and integration are inverse processes.
One breaks down, the other adds up.
They form the foundation of calculus.
animations: Display the derivative and integral symbols #FFFFFF.
Animate a bridge connecting these two concepts #FFFF00.
Show how they reverse each other's effects #FF0000.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Language of Change
lecture_lines: Calculus studies continuous change in our world.
It predicts the behavior of dynamic systems.
It is the core language of science.
animations: Reveal a complex system changing over time #00FFFF.
